title: Defending against Model Extraction for GNNs with Model Reprogramming

problem.claim: Black-box deployment of GNNs in MLaaS exposes them to model extraction attacks through API queries.

gap.claim: Existing defenses either transfer Euclidean or image-based strategies to graphs with severe utility degradation or fail to prevent theft in real time.

contributions.claim: GraphRP is a proactive defense framework that applies model reprogramming to protect GNNs against model extraction.
GraphRP uses a structure-aware gating mechanism driven by learnable topological prototypes to dynamically modulate the model's decision boundary.

Under bounded-loss, optimal-attacker, and local second-order assumptions, the authors prove a lower bound on attacker estimation error that increases with structural sensitivity of the reprogramming noise.

stated_novelty.claim: GraphRP differs from static perturbations by introducing a structure-aware gating mechanism based on learnable topological prototypes.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that GraphRP significantly degrades the effectiveness of hard-label and soft-label model extraction attacks.
The authors report that GraphRP preserves benign utility while degrading attack effectiveness.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs support high-stakes MLaaS applications but are exposed to model extraction through black-box APIs.
Existing defenses inadequately account for graph topology, degrade utility, or fail to prevent theft in real time.
GraphRP applies model reprogramming with a structure-aware gating mechanism based on learnable topological prototypes.
The structural firewall preserves fidelity for benign queries and increases Fisher Information along perturbation directions for adversarial queries.
The authors report theoretical protection guarantees and experimental degradation of hard-label and soft-label extraction attacks while preserving benign utility.

source_observation.claim: Defense mechanisms for graph models should account for topological dependencies rather than directly transferring image-oriented perturbation strategies.

interpretation.claim: Security interventions may need to be conditioned on the structure of the data domain to avoid trading away normal-use utility.

application.claim: For graph-based black-box services, investigate structure-aware, query-conditional defenses that distinguish benign and adversarial inputs.

exception.claim: The reported theoretical guarantee depends on bounded loss, an optimal attacker, and a local second-order approximation.

unknowns: Specific datasets, attack configurations, baselines, and quantitative results are not provided.
The abstract does not specify the implementation or training procedure for the topological prototypes and gating mechanism.
The scope of the theoretical lower bound beyond the stated assumptions is not described.
